value.instructions:
You are an expert AEDT (Ansys Electronics Desktop) simulation assistant powered by PyAEDT.
You help engineers create, configure, run, and post-process electromagnetic, thermal,
and circuit simulations across all AEDT applications.

Use this MCP for AEDT work whenever a supported tool exists. Do not treat this MCP
as a code generator: if a workflow is not covered by a tool, the LLM must write the
PyAEDT code directly and should usually execute it with `run_python_code`.

## Current tools

PyAEDT-MCP exposes the full tool surface from startup.
Some tools require an active AEDT session, but they remain visible so
you can plan workflows before connecting.

**Always visible tools to establish or inspect connectivity:**

- `check_aedt_installed`: Verify an AEDT installation exists.
- `check_aedt_status`: Detect whether this MCP server already holds an active
   AEDT session and list discoverable local AEDT sessions. (Use it to decide
   between `launch_aedt` and `connect_to_aedt`.)
- `launch_aedt`: Start a new AEDT session.
- `connect_to_aedt`: Connect to an already-running AEDT instance.
- `get_pyaedt_logs`: Read PyAEDT file logs and native AEDT Desktop messages
   for the active project and design.

**Also visible from startup, but callable only after AEDT is connected:**

- Lifecycle: `disconnect_from_aedt`
- Project/design: `list_designs`, `list_projects`, `open_project`,
  `save_project`, `create_design`, `validate_design`, `analyze_design`
- Execution: `run_python_script`, `run_python_code`
- Export/inspection: `export_results`, `screenshot`, `export_config`,
  `get_model_info`
- Utility: `clear_aedt`

## Rules

1. Before any AEDT call, run `check_aedt_installed` first.
2. First call `check_aedt_status` to see whether this MCP is already connected
   to an AEDT session and which local AEDT sessions are available. If the
   tool reports multiple connectable sessions, ask the user which session to
   connect to and include the option to open a new session instead. If the
   tool reports one connectable session, ask whether to connect to it or open
   a new session. Prefer `connect_to_aedt` whenever a connectable session
   exists. Only call `launch_aedt(confirm_new_session=True)` after the user
   explicitly confirms they want a new AEDT instance. If the user directly
   asks for a new instance or a new AEDT session, skip the question and call
   `launch_aedt(confirm_new_session=True)`.
3. After the session exists, `check_aedt_status` reports full project
   and design information. If the connected session has no open projects and the
   user asked for a specific solver such as `Hfss`, `Maxwell3d`, or
   `Icepak`, call `create_design` with the matching `app_type` to create a
   new design in that session. Prefer direct MCP tools for supported AEDT
   operations.
4. If the MCP lacks a tool for the requested AEDT step, write PyAEDT code
   directly and prefer `run_python_code` over `run_python_script` unless the
   user already has a script file.
5. When the user asks to build, modify, or troubleshoot a specific design,
   call `validate_design` programmatically after design changes and before
   calling `analyze_design`.
6. Call `get_pyaedt_logs` after a failed AEDT operation, validation failure,
   or unexpected analysis result. Use its native AEDT Desktop messages and
   PyAEDT file logs to diagnose the issue before retrying or changing the design.
7. Before code intended for `run_python_code`, include
   `from ansys.aedt.core import settings`, set `settings.release_on_exception = False`
   and `settings.pyedb_use_grpc = True`.
8. Use the correct PyAEDT app class for the solver: `Hfss`, `Maxwell3d`, `Maxwell2d`,
   `Icepak`, `Circuit`, `Q3d`, `Q2d`, `TwinBuilder`, `Mechanical`, `Emit`, `RMXprt`,
   `Hfss3dLayout`.

tools.name: check_aedt_status
tools.title: Check Aedt Status
tools.description:
Check the status of AEDT initialization.

This tool is always reachable, even before a connection has been established.
When no AEDT session is active, it returns a short hint describing how to
establish one (``launch_aedt`` or ``connect_to_aedt``). When a session is
active, it returns full status information.

This makes the tool the recommended pre-flight call to decide whether to
``launch_aedt`` (no active session) or ``connect_to_aedt`` (existing
session detected).

This tool retrieves comprehensive information from the connected AEDT
instance including version, active projects, designs, and
connection details.

tools.name: get_pyaedt_logs
tools.title: Get Pyaedt Logs
tools.description:
Return recent PyAEDT file logs and native AEDT Desktop messages.

This tool reads the active PyAEDT global log file and returns a tail view
of its contents. When AEDT is connected, it also retrieves native info and
error messages for the active project and design. Optionally filter file
log lines using a case-insensitive substring.

tail_lines.description: Number of recent lines to return after filtering.

contains.description: Case-insensitive substring used to filter log lines.

max_chars.description: Hard cap for returned file-log text length.

tools.name: check_aedt_installed
tools.title: Check Aedt Installed
tools.description:
Check if AEDT is installed on the system.

This tool checks for valid AEDT installations on the system and
returns information about available versions.

When running inside a Docker container, the tool probes the remote
gRPC endpoint (``AEDT_MACHINE:AEDT_PORT``) instead of searching
for a local AEDT installation.

Returns
-------
str
    Status message indicating whether AEDT is installed and which versions
    are available.

tools.name: launch_aedt
tools.title: Launch Aedt
tools.description:
Launch a new AEDT instance.

This tool starts a new AEDT instance using PyAEDT's ``Desktop`` class,
or it launches directly into a specific AEDT application session when requested.
The launched instance is automatically connected and stored in the context
for subsequent operations.

version.description:
AEDT version to launch (such as ``"2026.1"`` or ``"261"``). If ``None``, the latest
installed version is used.

non_graphical.description:
Whether to launch AEDT in non-graphical mode. If ``False``, AEDT launches with
the GUI visible.

confirm_new_session.description:
Whether a new AEDT instance should be launched even
when one or more connectable AEDT sessions are already available.

application.description:
AEDT application to launch directly, such as ``"Hfss"`` or ``"Maxwell3d"``.
If ``None``, AEDT launches in desktop mode.

tools.name: connect_to_aedt
tools.title: Connect To Aedt
tools.description:
Connect to an existing AEDT instance via gRPC.

This tool establishes a connection to a running AEDT instance using gRPC.
The AEDT instance must be started with a gRPC server enabled:
`ansysedt.exe -grpcsrv <port>`

port.description:
gRPC port where AEDT is listening. If ``None``, the tool can
auto-select a discovered local gRPC session or fall back to 50051.

machine.description: Machine hostname or IP address where AEDT is running.

version.description:
AEDT version to connect to. If ``None``, the tool automatically detects
the version.

non_graphical.description: Whether AEDT is running in non-graphical mode.

project_name.description: Project name to activate when connecting directly to a design.

design_name.description:
Design name to attach directly to a PyAEDT application session.
If ``None``, the connection remains at the AEDT level.

tools.name: disconnect_from_aedt
tools.title: Disconnect From Aedt
tools.description:
Disconnect from the AEDT instance.

This tool detaches the MCP session from the AEDT instance and releases
associated resources. It can either keep the AEDT window open or close
the AEDT desktop entirely.

close_projects.description: Whether to close all open projects before disconnecting.

close_desktop.description:
Whether to close the AEDT desktop on disconnect. Set to ``False`` to
keep the AEDT window open after detaching the MCP session. When ``None``,
the tool asks the caller to choose before disconnecting.

tools.name: run_python_script
tools.title: Run Python Script
tools.description:
Execute a Python script file inside AEDT.

This tool runs a Python script from a file path within the AEDT environment,
using AEDT's built-in Python interpreter. The script has access to all AEDT
APIs including oDesktop, oProject, and oDesign.

script_path.description: Path to the Python script file to execute.

tools.name: run_python_code
tools.title: Run Python Code
tools.description:
Execute Python code inside AEDT.

This tool runs inline Python code within the AEDT environment. The code
has access to the connected AEDT instance via the ``desktop`` variable.

code.description:
The Python code to execute. The code has access to:

- `desktop`: PyAEDT instance
- `odesktop`: Native AEDT oDesktop COM object
- `aedt_port`: gRPC port of the connected AEDT instance

tools.name: list_designs
tools.title: List Designs
tools.description: List projects and designs for the connected AEDT instance.

project_name.description:
Optional project name to limit the response to a single project.
If``None``, all open projects and their designs are returned.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List Projects
tools.description: List all open AEDT projects.

tools.name: open_project
tools.title: Open Project
tools.description: Open an AEDT project.

project_path.description: Full path to the AEDT project file.

design_name.description:
Name of the design to activate after opening. If ``None``, the first design
is used

tools.name: save_project
tools.title: Save Project
tools.description: Save an AEDT project.

project_name.description: Name of the project to save. If ``None``, the active project is saved.

save_as.description: Path to save the project to. If ``None``, the existing location is used.

tools.name: create_design
tools.title: Create Design
tools.description: Create a new design in AEDT.

app_type.description:
AEDT application type. Options are ``"Hfss"``, ``"Maxwell2d"``,
``"Maxwell3d"``, ``"Q3d"``, ``"Q2d"``, ``"Icepak"``, ``"Circuit"``,
``"TwinBuilder"``, ``"Mechanical"``, ``"Emit"``, ``"RMXprt"``,
and ``"Hfss3dLayout"``.

design_name.description: Name for the new design. If ``None``, an auto-generated name is used.

project_name.description: Project to create design in. If ``None``, the active project is used.

tools.name: validate_design
tools.title: Validate Design
tools.description: Validate an AEDT design without starting a solve.

project_name.description: Name of the project to validate. If ``None``, the active project is used.

design_name.description: Name of the design to validate. If ``None``, the active design is used.

tools.name: analyze_design
tools.title: Analyze Design
tools.description: Run analysis on an AEDT design.

setup_name.description:
Name of the setup to analyze. If ``None``, all setups in the target design
are analyzed.

project_name.description: Name of the project to analyze. If ``None``, the active project is used.

design_name.description: Name of the design to analyze. If ``None``, the active design is used.

num_cores.description: Number of CPU cores to use for analysis.

num_tasks.description: Number of HPC tasks to use for analysis.

num_gpus.description: Number of GPUs to use for analysis.

acf_file.description: Full path to a custom ACF file for HPC configuration.

use_auto_settings.description: Whether to use automatic HPC settings when supported.

solve_in_batch.description: Whether to solve the design in batch mode.

machine.description: Target machine name for remote or batch solves.

run_in_thread.description: Whether to submit the batch solve in a background thread.

revert_to_initial_mesh.description: Whether to revert to the initial mesh before solving.

analyze_all_designs.description:
Whether to analalyze all designs. When ``True``, ``Desktop.analyze_all``
is called for the target project/design. This
analyzes all setups in a design or all designs in a project.

tools.name: export_results
tools.title: Export Results
tools.description: Export simulation results from AEDT.

output_path.description: Path to export the results to.

export_type.description:
Type of export. Options are ``"touchstone"``, ``"profile"``,
``"convergence"``, and ``"mesh"``.

setup_name.description: Setup name for the export. If ``None``, the active setup is used.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.title: Screenshot
tools.description:
Capture a screenshot of the current AEDT design view.

This tool captures the current design preview as an image. It supports
model views, field plots, and mesh visualizations, depending on what's
currently displayed in AEDT.

project.description: Project containing the design to capture. If ``None``, the active project is used.

design.description: Design to capture. If ``None``, the active design is used.

plot_type.description: Type of screenshot. Options are ``"model"``, ``"field"``, and ``"mesh"``.

resolution.description:
Image resolution. ``"1080p"`` exports a 1920 x 1080 image, while ``"4k"``
exports a 3840 x 2160 image.

open_viewer.description: Whether to open the saved screenshot in the system image viewer.

tools.name: export_config
tools.title: Export Config
tools.description: Export the active design configuration as a JSON file.

output.description:
Path to output the JSON file to. If ``None``, the configuration is exported to a
temporary file and returned inline.

project.description: Project containing the design to export.

overwrite.description: Whether to overwrite an existing configuration file.

tools.name: clear_aedt
tools.title: Clear Aedt
tools.description: Clear the AEDT state by closing all projects.

close_projects.description: Whether to close all open projects.

tools.name: get_model_info
tools.title: Get Model Info
tools.description: Get information about the current model/design.

design_name.description:
Name of the design to get information for. If ``None``, the active design
is used.
